fieldData.guide-section-heading: Instagram influencer marketing: a guide for brands
fieldData.guide-section-content:
What Instagram influencer marketing involves

Instagram influencer marketing means paying creators to feature your product in Reels, Stories or feed posts for their followers. You choose the creators, agree the deliverables and the fee, review the content, then pay. A campaign can be one post from one creator or an ongoing partnership with many.

Three ways to hire Instagram creators

Do it yourselfAgencyJem Social
Finding creatorsSearch Instagram by hand and keep a spreadsheetThe agency builds the listFilter by niche, city, followers and engagement
Contact detailsFrom bios or DMsThrough the agencyEach creator's email
Audience dataAsk each creator for screenshotsAgency reportsAudience data on each profile
Paying creatorsInvoices or payment appsThrough the agencyThrough Jem, held until you approve the content
CostYour time, plus creator ratesAgency fees, plus creator rates$69/month, billed monthly, after a 7-day free trial, plus creator rates

Looking for an Instagram influencer agency? An agency makes sense if you want someone else to run the whole campaign. If you'd rather pick the creators yourself, a platform handles the search, outreach and payment.

See how Jem Social's price compares with 7 other platforms.

How to choose Instagram creators

  • Engagement rate for their size. Compare creators in the same follower range, not against the whole market. The Engagement Rate Calculator works it out from any public profile.
  • Audience. Check where a creator's followers live and how old they are, so their audience matches your buyers. Jem Social shows audience data on each profile.
  • Recent content. Look at their latest posts and past brand deals. Is it the quality you'd run in your own ads?
  • Niche fit. A creator whose followers already care about your category needs less explaining.
  • A real following. Look for steady follower growth, comments from real people, and posts that match what the creator says they do.

What Instagram creators cost

Rates depend on followers, deliverables and usage rights, so there's no single price. The Influencer Rate Calculator gives a starting point, and each creator's rate estimate is in Jem Social. Agree on deliverables and usage rights before any content is made.

Disclosure and the paid partnership label

The FTC says an endorsement should make it obvious when the creator has a relationship with the brand. The disclosure should sit with the endorsement itself, not only on a profile page or behind a "more" link, and the FTC says not to assume a platform's disclosure tool is enough on its own. (FTC: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers, checked November 9, 2026.)

On Instagram, all branded content must be disclosed with the paid partnership label, which lets a creator tag up to two brands in Feed, Stories, Reels and Live. (Instagram Help Center, paid partnership label, checked November 9, 2026.)

Put both in your brief: ask creators to use the label and to say it in the post. This is general information, not legal advice.

Running your first Instagram campaign

  1. Write a brief: the product, deliverables, talking points, budget and deadline. The Campaign Brief Generator gives you a template.
  2. Shortlist creators in Jem Social and message them.
  3. Agree on rates, deliverables, usage rights and the paid partnership label.
  4. Review the content. Payment is released once you approve it.
  5. Measure the results with the Influencer Marketing ROI Calculator.

Hiring on more than one platform? See the TikTok influencer marketing guide, which includes Jem Social's numbers on US TikTok creators by follower range.
